A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same graphon-mixture learning framework. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v3 reports original synthetic clustering experiments, GMAM and MGCL benchmark results, runtime measurements, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains these original results and adds experiments on graph-size-dependent moment concentration and MGCL component contributions.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1–3 retain the same motif clustering, graphon estimation, GMAM generation, and MGCL augmentation and loss procedures. GIA/CAL terminology and suggestions for choosing K clarify existing components without establishing an implemented method change.

E1.justification: New Appendix F.2 extends synthetic evaluation to very small graphs with 5 and 10 nodes, alongside 100- and 300-node graphs. This adds a small-graph test scenario beyond the retained synthetic settings of 75–300 or 200 nodes. Real-world dataset and task coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: New Table 12 evaluates MGCL without CAL, using graphon-informed augmentation with standard InfoNCE, alongside GraphCL and full MGCL. This adds an explicit comparison variant; comparator membership in the existing benchmark tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix F.2 introduces a controlled design using three graphons and 40 graphs per graphon at each of four node counts. Appendix F.7 adds sequential component controls. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, architectures, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds targeted analyses isolating graph size's effect on moment concentration and measuring GIA's contribution followed by CAL's incremental contribution on three datasets. Existing motif-count, cluster-number, mixture-count, estimation-quality, and false-negative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The existing ± reporting, eight-run mixup statement, shared-seed information, and ten-trial MGCL cluster ablation are unchanged. Table 12 extends the existing ± presentation without introducing a new uncertainty procedure, significance test, or run-count disclosure.

E6.justification: Table 12 newly reports GIA-only accuracies of 74.79%, 88.29%, and 71.38% on PROTEINS, MUTAG, and IMDB-B, respectively. Appendix F.2 reports greater overlap for small graphs and stronger concentration for larger graphs. Existing benchmark scores and retained appendix results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 qualifies the inference from large empirical motif differences to large graphon cut distance by requiring sufficiently small sampling error; v3 states that implication without this explicit condition. The theorem statements and proofs in Appendices B and C remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and principal conclusions retain the same mixture-estimation, GMAM, and MGCL contributions and performance claims. The conclusion rephrases the novelty statement without materially changing its meaning.

C2.justification: v3 briefly discusses small-graph sampling noise. v4 substantially expands applicability boundaries: Appendix F.1 explains failure of truncated motif families, and Appendix G limits the dense-graphon interpretation, discusses sparse extensions, and interprets sparse-benchmark graphons as approximations. It also adds explanations of cluster-level averaging and the complementary GIA/CAL contributions.

D1.justification: Section 4 newly reports code availability and provides a repository address, absent from v3. Existing implementation, optimizer, software, and hardware disclosures remain unchanged. Repository contents and accessibility are not established by the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: v4 adds three Borgs and colleagues references on sparse graph limits and exchangeable graphs to position possible sparse extensions. GCN and DropEdge bibliography updates refer to the same existing works and do not introduce new research comparisons.

P1.justification: v4 makes targeted method and conclusion edits, adds scope, impact, and conflict-of-interest sections, and updates conference front matter. It corrects the erroneous MGCL/GMAM expansions and Table 9 reference in the appendix. Most prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds Figure 5 and Table 12, simplifies Table 9's header and caption, and relocates existing tables and appendix figures. Retained graphics preserve their content. The new graph-size plot lacks an explicit legend mapping marker sizes to node counts.

improvement.justification: Table 12 supplies targeted evidence about MGCL's components, while Section 3.1 and Appendix G better explain when graphon separation and dense-graphon interpretations are justified. The code-access statement and editorial corrections also help readers. Figure 5's incomplete size labeling limits that addition's clarity, but the improved supporting evidence and applicability discussion establish a limited net improvement.
